---
title: Search
icon: Search
description: "Full-text search over your documents: named indexes, relevance ranking, snippets and synonym expansion, built on PostgreSQL full-text search."
---

import { Database, Boxes, LineChart, Sparkles } from 'lucide-react';

Search gives your app a full-text index it can query for relevance rather than
exact matches. You create a named **index**, push **documents** into it, and
query with a phrase; Applad returns ranked **hits** with a highlighted snippet.
It lives under `/v1/search` and is backed by PostgreSQL full-text search, so
there is no separate search engine to run.

<Callout title="Project-scoped and authenticated">
Every route below requires the project header `x-applad-project` and an
authenticated caller: a client sends the session bearer token, a server sends
its API key `x-applad-key`.
</Callout>

## Create an index

An index is a container for documents. Give it a `name`; you can pass your own
`indexId` or let one be generated.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Node.js', 'Python', 'cURL']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await client.search.createIndex('articles', { name: 'Articles' });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```ts
await server.search.createIndex('articles', { name: 'Articles' });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
client.search.create_index("articles", name="Articles")
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="cURL">
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/search/indexes \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"indexId":"articles","name":"Articles"}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Underlying route: `POST /v1/search/indexes`. `name` is required. The response is
the index:

```json
{
  "$id": "articles",
  "name": "Articles",
  "fields": ["content"],
  "typoTolerance": false,
  "status": "ready"
}
```

List, fetch and delete indexes with `listIndexes()`, `getIndex(id)` and
`deleteIndex(id)` (`GET /v1/search/indexes`, `GET` and
`DELETE /v1/search/indexes/{indexId}`). Deleting an index removes its documents.

<Callout title="What actually gets searched">
An index stores a `fields` list and a `typoTolerance` flag, but the query path
searches a single derived **content** string per document and ranks it with
PostgreSQL `ts_rank`. When you index a document as structured `data`, Applad
builds that content from `data.content`, else `data.text`, else all string
values joined together. Give a document a `content` field to control exactly
what is searchable.
</Callout>

## Index a document

Push a document under a `documentId` you choose. Re-indexing the same
`documentId` replaces it (upsert).

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Python', 'cURL']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
await client.search.indexDocument('articles', 'post-1', {
  content: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog',
  title: 'A fox story',
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
client.search.index_document("articles", "post-1", {
    "content": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
    "title": "A fox story",
})
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="cURL">
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/search/indexes/articles/documents \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"documentId":"post-1","data":{"content":"The quick brown fox","title":"A fox story"}}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Route: `POST /v1/search/indexes/{indexId}/documents` with `documentId` and a
`data` object. There is also
`PUT /v1/search/indexes/{indexId}/documents/{docId}` which takes a raw
`content` string plus optional `metadata`, and
`DELETE /v1/search/indexes/{indexId}/documents/{docId}` to remove one.

## Query

Query with a phrase. Results are ranked by relevance, each with a `score` and a
`snippet` cut around the match.

<Tabs items={['JavaScript', 'Node.js', 'Python', 'cURL']}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```ts
const res = await client.search.query('articles', 'brown fox', { limit: 20 });
for (const hit of res.hits) {
  console.log(hit.documentId, hit.score, hit.snippet);
}
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Node.js">
```ts
const res = await server.search.query('articles', 'brown fox', { limit: 20 });
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python
res = client.search.query("articles", "brown fox", limit=20)
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="cURL">
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/search/indexes/articles/search \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"query":"brown fox","limit":20}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Routes: `POST /v1/search/indexes/{indexId}/search` (or `/query`), and a
convenience `GET /v1/search/indexes/{indexId}/query?q=brown+fox`. The response
is a ranked result set:

```json
{
  "total": 1,
  "processingTimeMs": "0.83ms",
  "hits": [
    {
      "documentId": "post-1",
      "content": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
      "metadata": { "title": "A fox story" },
      "score": 0.12,
      "snippet": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog"
    }
  ]
}
```

The body accepts `query`, `limit` (default 20, max 500) and `offset`. Ranking
uses the English text-search configuration; if a document has no full-text
match, the query falls back to a substring match so a partial word still finds
something.

## Synonyms

A synonym group tells the index that a set of words mean the same thing. When a
query contains any word in a group, the query is expanded with the others before
ranking, so a search for "car" also matches "automobile".

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.applad.io/v1/search/indexes/articles/synonyms \
  -H "x-applad-project: <projectId>" -H "x-applad-key: <apiKey>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"synonyms":["car","automobile","vehicle"]}'
```

Routes: `POST` / `GET /v1/search/indexes/{indexId}/synonyms` (a group needs at
least two words) and `DELETE /v1/search/indexes/{indexId}/synonyms/{synId}`.
Synonyms are managed over HTTP; the SDK `search` service covers indexes,
documents and querying.

<Callout title="Scope and scale">
Search is a lightweight, built-in index meant to save you from bolting on a
separate service for typical app search. Ranking rules and typo tolerance are
recorded on an index but are not applied by the query engine today, and search
matches the derived content string rather than per-field. For semantic or
nearest-neighbour matching over embeddings, use [Vectors](/build/vectors).
</Callout>
